decision: Keep both native-map React Compiler diagnostic groups deferred.
status: Deferred optimization; no correctness defect established by this audit.

diagnostics.interpretation: The compiler conservatively flags refs passed through lazy initialization. The Mapbox group includes registry and handle initialization; MapLibre includes handle initialization.

rationale: The inspected factories retain refs and callbacks for later commands. No render-time current read was established.
The Mapbox registry constructor stores its reset callback through NativeFeatureState without invoking it.
Handles must retain attachment identity and read current wrapper refs when commands run. MapLibre also gates camera commands on map-load readiness.
No small behavior-preserving rewrite tested in memory enabled compilation. Moving creation into effects would require reviewing handle availability and attachment ordering.

auditEvidence.scan: Babel transformSync over all committed library TypeScript sources at the recorded revision, using target 19 and CompileError logging from the installed compiler. Diagnostic grouping matches scripts/react-compiler.mjs.
auditEvidence.factoryProbe: The current emitted createMapboxMapRef and createMaplibreMapRef received refs whose current getters throw. Construction performed zero reads; later jumpTo calls read those getters and rejected. Constructing the Mapbox registry did not invoke its reset callback.
auditEvidence.factoryProbeArtifact: Emitted modules from the passing library build recorded in records/evidence/react-compiler-lifecycle-cleanups.json; no build was repeated during the read-only audit.

alternatives.outcome: Ref diagnostics remain. It does not preserve state-owned lifetime guarantees as a replacement.
Ref diagnostics remain, including additional render-time access reports.

alternatives.candidate: Inline the full handle object while retaining existing refs and callback bindings
alternatives.outcome: Ref diagnostics remain. Unlike the small facade proxy, this does not enable compilation.

consequences: Both native-map components continue without compiler optimization. This record does not measure the performance cost.
Existing behavior, public signatures, source registries, capture ownership and command readiness remain unchanged.

revisit.owner: Maintainer changing the compiler configuration or either native adapter.
triggers: A compiler upgrade or analysis change may recognize deferred ref captures; rerun the exact component compilation probes.
Profiling identifies material repeated work in either skipped native-map component.
A separately justified handle, registry or capture lifecycle change creates a smaller initialization boundary.
A regression establishes an actual render-time ref read, stale handle, readiness failure or ownership error.
completionCriteria: The exact affected native-map implementation reports CompileSuccess without hiding or relocating its diagnostic to another hook.
Preserve stable handles and registries across rerenders, fresh ownership on remount and rejection of commands retained from detached attachments.
Preserve MapLibre map-load readiness, capture scope and teardown, camera command observation, committed callback behavior and feature-state queue/reset ordering.
Add regressions for any changed boundary and run applicable formatting, documentation, type, source, mocked native, library-build and compiled-output checks.
Assess affected runtime acceptance separately. Obtain explicit permission before renderer tests or native acceptance builds/installations.

limitations: Routine component suites, native builds, renderer acceptance and performance benchmarks were not run for this deferral record.
The source review and isolated factory probe do not renew runtime acceptance or prove all possible ref-related failures absent.
